Current player engine: %1$s. Most users should leave the profile on Auto. Light targets lower-end devices, combines stability choices from the former Compatible profile with lower fixed resource budgets, and replaces that separate profile. Engine-specific decode, output, and protocol controls remain available below for unusual devices and create a Custom profile when changed. Most low-level changes take effect after playback restarts or the player is rebuilt.

Balanced is merged into Auto by default. Legacy Balanced selections are migrated independently for EXO, MPV and IJK, while Compatible, Light and Custom selections are preserved. Local rollback restores only migrated engines that still remain on Auto; choices made after migration are not overwritten. The historical A/B report stays available, but real device acceptance has not been established by build or JVM tests.

The Balanced tab will return. Engines migrated from Balanced will be restored only if they are still on Auto. Compatible, Light or Custom choices made after migration will not be changed. A/B collection remains off until you explicitly enroll again.

Legacy Balanced selections will be migrated to Auto independently for each engine and the Balanced tab will be hidden. Existing A/B samples are retained, while new collection is disabled. Compatible, Light and Custom choices are preserved.

This is an internal, device-local observational V-06A assessment. It is off by default, has no user-facing enrollment entry and never randomizes profiles. It observes only the selected Auto or Light profile, and admits only hardware-decoded sessions on low-RAM devices or sessions that actually use software decoding. Internal experiment authorization and the current engine domain must both be enabled. Passing only permits a further product review; it never hides or removes Light automatically.

Samples stay on this device, are not uploaded or backed up, and never switch profiles automatically. Only low-RAM hardware decoding or actual software decoding enters the report. Every valid group needs at least 20 usable Auto and 20 usable Light samples. Pause, seek, speed changes, profile changes and experimental interventions invalidate the current sample.

Groups: %4$d
Evaluable groups: %5$d
Passed: %6$d
Failed: %7$d
Insufficient or missing: %8$d

Further retention review requires all six EXO, MPV and IJK low-RAM hardware/software cells and every group to pass. This report never removes the Light profile automatically.
All device-local Auto/Light assessment samples will be deleted. Enrollment remains and eligible sessions can be collected again. The historical Auto/Balanced A/B report is unaffected.

V-06B is a fail-closed audit of whether the Compatible profile can ever be reconsidered. It checks EXO, MPV and IJK coverage for codec failures, hardware capability misreporting, output-mode faults, and protocol/Range faults, plus visual-correctness detection and long-term problem-device evidence. Existing recovery is bounded and depends on explicit errors or observable metrics. Green screens, wrong colors or an incorrect picture without a decoder error cannot currently be detected reliably, so the present conclusion is to retain Compatible. This report never hides, migrates or removes a profile.

Current conclusion: %1$s
Reliable coverage: %2$d / %3$d
Limited: %4$d
Unverified: %5$d
Unobservable: %6$d
Missing: %7$d

Every requirement must have reliable automated recovery and long-term device evidence before further review. Even full coverage would only permit another product decision; this report never removes Compatible automatically.

This internal collection is off by default, has no user-facing enrollment entry and stays on this device. It observes only the selected Auto or balanced profile; it never randomizes or changes profiles. Samples are admitted only while internal experiment authorization and the current engine domain are enabled. They store bounded numeric metrics and enum/digest grouping facts, never URLs, hosts, paths, headers, raw fingerprints or decoder names. The report cannot merge or migrate profiles automatically.

Device-local, opt-in infrastructure for comparing Auto and balanced within the same device, engine, decoder, protocol, stream, MIME/HDR and path group. Successful samples require at least 30 seconds of valid playback; attributable playback errors can be retained to avoid survivor bias. Data expires after 30 days and is bounded. The report needs at least 20 usable samples per arm for every group and never changes a profile.
